p: Getting to the Metrocentre is easy whichever way you travel. It has its own railway station, a busy bus station and huge car parks right off the A1, so you can pick whatever suits your crew. Parking is plentiful, but on busy Saturdays and in the run-up to Christmas the roads around the centre can be slow, so leave a little extra time.

Before you climb, everyone will need a participation form, signed by a parent or guardian for under-18s. Do it online on the way and you'll get through check-in quicker. Check the age guidance when you book too, as there's usually a minimum age for climbers and rules about supervising little ones.

Allow a couple of hours for the climb itself, including the safety briefing and harness fitting, then plan the shopping or food around it. A clever move is to climb first and eat after, as climbing on a full stomach isn't much fun.

If you'd rather get out of the shops afterwards, Gateshead has some brilliant places to visit. Saltwell Park is a grand Victorian park with a boating lake, gardens and plenty of play space. Down on the Quayside, the Baltic Centre for Contemporary Art is free to visit and has cracking views over the Tyne from its upper floors, and The Glasshouse music venue sits right alongside, under its curved glass roof.
